children.title: Weak Gram Feasibility
children.top_down_role: Feasibility without a strictly positive-definite Gram representative.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Gram Feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tolerance-dependent Gram feasibility used by numerical recognition procedures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a Gram coefficient system \(\mathcal{A}(Q)=b\), norm \(\|\cdot\|\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), weak Gram feasibility holds when there exists \(Q\in\mathbb{S}^N\) such that \(\|\mathcal{A}(Q)-b\|\le\varepsilon\) and \(\lambda_{\min}(Q)\ge-\varepsilon\). This condition accepts bounded violations of both coefficient equality and positive semidefiniteness. It is a numerical predicate, not an exact SOS certificate; exact feasibility follows only if a limit or recovered matrix satisfies \(\mathcal{A}(Q)=b\) and \(Q\succeq0\) exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak Gram feasibility allows bounded coefficient residual and negative eigenvalue error, but does not itself certify exact SOS membership.
assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon>0\) and a residual norm are fixed.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: residual-and-cone-distance definition of numerical weak feasibility
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a coherent tolerance-dependent numerical predicate, but weak feasibility terminology and the use of the same epsilon for residual and eigenvalue violations vary across sources and require an explicit convention or citation.

children.title: Facial-Reduction Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Structural identification of proper semidefinite faces containing feasible Gram slices.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^m\to\mathbb R^q\) is linear and \(F=\{Q\succeq0:\mathcal A(Q)=b\}\neq\varnothing\).
An exposing vector \(Z\succeq0\) satisfies \(\langle Z,Q\rangle=0\) for every \(Q\in F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\subseteq\mathbb S_+^m\cap Z^\perp=\{Q\succeq0:\operatorname{range}(Q)\subseteq\ker Z\}\), a proper face when \(Z\neq0\).

notation.meaning: Real symmetric matrices and their positive-semidefinite cone.
Orthogonal complement of the span of the exposing matrix.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step facial-reduction certificate for a positive-semidefinite Gram feasibility system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the feasible Gram set \(F=\{Q\in\mathbb S_+^m:\mathcal A(Q)=b\}\), a matrix \(Z\in\mathbb S_+^m\) is a facial-reduction diagnostic if \(Z\neq0\) and \(\langle Z,Q\rangle=0\) for every \(Q\in F\). Positivity implies \(Z^{1/2}QZ^{1/2}=0\), hence \(\operatorname{range}(Q)\subseteq\ker Z\). Therefore every feasible Gram matrix lies in the proper exposed face \(\mathbb S_+^m\cap Z^\perp\). Restricting subsequent feasibility tests to this face removes directions that cannot contain feasible points; repeated exposure terminates after at most \(m\) strict face reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero positive-semidefinite matrix orthogonal to every feasible Gram matrix exposes a smaller face containing the feasible set and diagnoses failure of strict feasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Facial-Reduction Diagnostics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role fits the diagnostic leaf and the face-containment statement is mathematically sound. However, the cited general face-geometry section does not adequately support the facial-reduction interpretation, strict-feasibility diagnosis, or the claim that repeated strict reductions terminate after at most m steps. A facial-reduction or semidefinite-feasibility source with a specific theorem or section is required.

children.title: Numerical Indistinguishability Near the Boundary
children.top_down_role: Difficulty separating weak feasibility, near-feasibility, and infeasibility using finite precision.

assumptions_latex: \(S=\{Q\in\mathbb S^m:\mathcal A(Q)=b\}\) is a nonempty affine space.
Distance is measured in a fixed matrix norm, with \(d=\inf_{Q\in S}\operatorname{dist}(Q,\mathbb S_+^m)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(d\le2\varepsilon\), then the \(\varepsilon\)-neighborhoods of \(S\) and \(\mathbb S_+^m\) intersect, so residual information at absolute accuracy \(\varepsilon\) cannot separate them uniformly.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: intersecting uncertainty neighborhoods give a norm-independent information-theoretic ambiguity criterion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute-error indistinguishability criterion for affine Gram feasibility near the semidefinite boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d=\inf\{\|Q-P\|:Q\in S,\ P\in\mathbb S_+^m\}\). If \(d\le2\varepsilon\), there exist \(Q\in S\) and \(P\succeq0\) whose closed \(\varepsilon\)-balls intersect. Consequently, an observation known only within absolute error \(\varepsilon\) can be consistent both with the affine constraints and with positive semidefiniteness, even when \(S\cap\mathbb S_+^m=\varnothing\). Thus no decision rule using only such uncertain residual data can uniformly distinguish feasibility from infeasibility on instances with separation at most \(2\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When an affine Gram space and the semidefinite cone are closer than twice the numerical uncertainty, residual data alone cannot reliably distinguish feasibility from infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Numerical Indistinguishability Near the Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, but no source is supplied and the stated implication is not valid without an attainment hypothesis at d=2 epsilon. If the distance infimum is not attained, d=2 epsilon need not yield intersecting closed epsilon-neighborhoods. A reliable version should use d<2 epsilon or assume attainment, and it needs a specific weak-feasibility or numerical distinguishability source.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^m\) is a Gram matrix with eigenvalues \(\lambda_1(Q)\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_m(Q)\ge0\).
A relative threshold \(\tau\in(0,1)\) is fixed and \(Q\neq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Near-rank deficiency is diagnosed by \(\lambda_m(Q)\le\tau\lambda_1(Q)\); the numerical rank is \(r_\tau(Q)=\#\{i:\lambda_i(Q)>\tau\lambda_1(Q)\}\).

notation.meaning: Ordered eigenvalues of the Gram matrix.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: relative eigenvalue threshold is the conventional spectral definition of numerical rank
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral, scale-invariant diagnosis for positive-semidefinite Gram matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonzero matrix \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^m\) is near-rank deficient at relative threshold \(\tau\in(0,1)\) when \(\lambda_m(Q)\le\tau\lambda_1(Q)\). Its thresholded numerical rank is \(r_\tau(Q)=\#\{i:\lambda_i(Q)>\tau\lambda_1(Q)\}\). If \(r_\tau(Q)<m\), then \(Q\) lies within spectral-norm distance at most \(\tau\lambda_1(Q)\) of a positive-semidefinite matrix of rank \(r_\tau(Q)\), obtained by setting the smaller eigenvalues to zero. This condition is invariant under positive rescaling of \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Gram matrix is near-rank deficient when its smallest eigenvalue is small relative to its largest; thresholding the spectrum gives its numerical rank.
knowledge_statements.title: Near-Rank Deficiency

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the leaf, and the thresholded-rank and spectral-distance claims are internally consistent. The designation of lambda_m(Q) <= tau lambda_1(Q) as near-rank deficiency is a threshold-dependent numerical convention, however, and no numerical linear algebra source with a specific locator is supplied.

assumptions_latex: \(p(x)=v(x)^\mathsf TQv(x)\) is intended as an SOS certificate with \(Q\succeq0\).
Floating-point data \(\widehat Q\) have coefficient residual \(\rho=\|\mathcal A(\widehat Q)-p\|\) and semidefinite defect \(\delta=\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(\widehat Q)\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unless exact or validated bounds prove \(\rho=0\) and \(\delta=0\), \(\widehat Q\) alone is not a rigorous SOS certificate for \(p\).

notation.meaning: Linear map from a Gram matrix to polynomial coefficients.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical boundary between approximate solver output and a rigorous SOS certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A floating-point matrix \(\widehat Q\) is only an approximate Gram witness when either \(\rho=\|\mathcal A(\widehat Q)-p\|>0\) or \(\delta=\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(\widehat Q)\}>0\). Small values of \(\rho\) and \(\delta\) do not imply the exact identities \(\mathcal A(\widehat Q)=p\) and \(\widehat Q\succeq0\), especially near a singular face. Therefore unvalidated floating-point output cannot certify that \(p\) is SOS. Certification requires exact reconstruction or outward-rounded bounds that establish both coefficient equality and positive semidefiniteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Small floating-point residuals and tiny negative eigenvalues do not prove an exact SOS identity; exact reconstruction or validated bounds are required.
knowledge_statements.title: Floating-Point Certificate Failure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind is appropriate and the distinction between approximate solver output and an exact SOS certificate is mathematically reasonable. The cited general numerical-comments section does not specifically support Gram residuals, semidefinite defects, exact SOS certification, or validated reconstruction. A dedicated SOS certification or validated semidefinite-computation source is required.

assumptions_latex: \(p\in\mathbb Q[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) and \(v\) is a finite monomial vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact verification of \(\mathcal A(Q)=p\) and \(Q\succeq0\) certifies \(p\in\Sigma[x]\).

notation.meaning: Cone of sums of squares of real polynomials.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the Gram characterization of SOS polynomials directly yields the exact rational certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact rational membership certificate for the SOS cone in a fixed monomial basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A rational Gram certificate for \(p\in\mathbb Q[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) is a matrix \(Q\in\mathbb S^m(\mathbb Q)\) satisfying \(p(x)=v(x)^\mathsf TQv(x)\) coefficientwise and \(Q\succeq0\). The identity is checked by exact rational arithmetic. Positive semidefiniteness may be checked by an exact factorization \(Q=L D L^\mathsf T\) with \(D\) diagonal and nonnegative, or by exact principal-minor criteria. These checks certify \(p\in\Sigma[x]\); when the factorization is rational, it also yields an explicit weighted rational-square decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact rational positive-semidefinite Gram matrix whose coefficient expansion equals the polynomial is a verifiable SOS membership certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Rational Gram Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind exactly fits this leaf, and the rational Gram characterization and exact checks are standard and precise. No inspectable source with a section, theorem, definition, or page locator is supplied, so the Gram characterization and exact positive-semidefiniteness criteria remain unsupported at this review layer.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The decomposition is a valid SOS certificate exactly when exact expansion gives \(p-\sum_{j=1}^s c_jh_j^2=0\) and every \(c_j\ge0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: polynomial identity testing by exact coefficient comparison is elementary and the SOS implication is definitional
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact verification procedure for an explicitly supplied weighted SOS decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(p\), nonnegative rational weights \(c_j\), and rational polynomials \(h_j\), compute \(r=p-\sum_{j=1}^s c_jh_j^2\) using exact polynomial arithmetic. Collect coefficients in a common monomial ordering and test \([x^\alpha]r=0\) for every exponent \(\alpha\) occurring in \(r\). Also verify \(c_j\ge0\) for every \(j\). Accept precisely when all coefficient tests and sign tests succeed; then output the checked identity \(p=\sum_{j=1}^s c_jh_j^2\). Otherwise output the first nonzero residual coefficient or negative weight as a rejection witness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expand the proposed rational square decomposition exactly, compare every coefficient with the target polynomial, and verify that all weights are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.title: Symbolic SOS Decomposition Checks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the terminal container, and exact coefficient comparison plus nonnegative-weight checks correctly verifies the supplied weighted-square identity. A specific symbolic SOS or exact polynomial-arithmetic source is nevertheless absent.

assumptions_latex: \([Q]\) is a symmetric interval matrix and \(p\) is an exact polynomial.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A verified point matrix \(Q\in[Q]\) satisfying \(\mathcal A(Q)=p\) and a rigorous bound \(\lambda_{\min}(Q)\ge0\) certify that \(p\) is SOS.

notation.meaning: Entrywise symmetric interval enclosure of Gram matrices.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validated-numerics interface for converting an approximate Gram witness into a rigorous certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An interval-validated Gram check must establish the existence of a point matrix \(Q\in[Q]\) satisfying the exact affine equations \(\mathcal A(Q)=p\), for example by a verified linear-system inclusion test, and must prove \(Q\succeq0\). The latter may be established by an outward-rounded lower bound \(\underline\lambda\le\lambda_{\min}(Q)\) with \(\underline\lambda\ge0\), or by a verified positive-semidefinite factorization. If both validations succeed, then \(p(x)=v(x)^\mathsf TQv(x)\) is rigorously SOS. Merely finding zero inside every residual interval is not an existence proof.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Validated interval checks must prove one enclosed matrix satisfies the exact coefficient equations and is positive semidefinite; componentwise residual containment alone is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.title: Interval-Validated Gram Checks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind is compatible with the validation leaf, and the statement correctly distinguishes residual interval containment from proof that one enclosed matrix satisfies all equations. The cited basic interval-arithmetic section does not support the required verified linear inclusion, eigenvalue, factorization, or Gram-certificate assertions. A validated numerics source addressing these tests is required.

assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional inner-product space and \(y\) is the candidate point.
A proposed witness \(z\in K^*=\{z:\langle z,x\rangle\ge0\ \forall x\in K\}\) is exactly representable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequalities \(z\in K^*\) and \(\langle z,y\rangle<0\) certify \(y\notin K\).

notation.meaning: Closed convex cone whose membership is tested.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: weak separation by an element of the dual cone is a direct convex-duality certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact separating-hyperplane certificate for nonmembership in a closed convex cone, including an SOS cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be a closed convex cone and \(y\) a candidate member. A dual nonmembership certificate is an exactly verifiable vector \(z\in K^*\) such that \(\langle z,y\rangle<0\). Indeed, every \(x\in K\) satisfies \(\langle z,x\rangle\ge0\), so the strict negative pairing excludes \(y\) from \(K\). For a Gram-represented SOS cone, \(z\) may be given as a linear functional whose associated moment or localizing matrix is positive semidefinite; exact verification must check both dual-cone membership and the strict sign of its evaluation on \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exactly verified dual-cone element that pairs negatively with the candidate is a separating certificate proving nonmembership.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Nonmembership Verification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The general dual-cone separation certificate is correct and the certificate kind fits the leaf. No conic-duality source is supplied, and the specialization to a moment or localizing matrix is insufficiently scoped: a moment matrix describes the dual of a fixed-degree SOS cone, while localizing matrices require a specified constrained quadratic module. A precise source and formulation are required.

assumptions_latex: Polynomials in \(n\) variables of degree at most \(2d\) are represented using all monomials of degree at most \(d\).
The Gram matrix is stored densely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Gram dimension is \(N=\binom{n+d}{d}\), requiring \(N(N+1)/2=\Theta(N^2)\) scalar matrix entries.

notation.meaning: Length of the dense monomial vector.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: stars-and-bars counts degree-bounded monomials and determines the dense symmetric Gram size
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation-size barrier for dense degree-(2d\) SOS Gram formulations as variable count grows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The monomial vector containing every monomial in \(n\) variables of total degree at most \(d\) has length \(N=\binom{n+d}{d}\). Hence a dense SOS representation \(p=v_d^\mathsf TQv_d\) uses an \(N\times N\) positive-semidefinite Gram matrix with \(N(N+1)/2\) independent scalar entries. For fixed \(d\), \(N=\Theta(n^d)\) as \(n\to\infty\), so dense Gram storage is \(\Theta(n^{2d})\). Thus increasing the variable count produces polynomial growth whose exponent is controlled by the relaxation degree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With fixed half-degree, the monomial basis grows like the variable count to that degree, while a dense Gram matrix needs the square of that many entries.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Count Barrier

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits the variable-count barrier. The monomial count, symmetric-entry count, and fixed-d asymptotics are correct under the stated dense representation assumptions, but no source with a specific locator is supplied.

assumptions_latex: Polynomials in \(n\) variables of degree at most \(2d\) use the dense monomial vector through degree \(d\).
The number of variables \(n\ge1\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Gram dimension \(N=\binom{n+d}{n}=\Theta(d^n)\), and dense storage is \(\Theta(d^{2n})\) as \(d\to\infty\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the degree-bounded monomial count gives the dense Gram dimension and storage asymptotics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation-size barrier for dense SOS Gram formulations as relaxation degree grows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed \(n\), the vector \(v_d\) of all monomials of total degree at most \(d\) has length \(N=\binom{n+d}{n}\). A dense degree-\(2d\) SOS Gram formulation therefore contains an \(N\times N\) positive-semidefinite block and \(N(N+1)/2\) independent matrix entries. As \(d\to\infty\), \(N=\Theta(d^n)\) and dense storage is \(\Theta(d^{2n})\). Consequently, raising the SOS or moment relaxation order rapidly enlarges the semidefinite representation even when the variable count remains fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed number of variables, increasing the SOS half-degree makes the Gram dimension grow like degree to the variable count and storage like its square.
knowledge_statements.title: Degree-Growth Barrier

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits the degree-growth barrier. The fixed-n monomial and storage asymptotics are correct for a dense Gram formulation, but the record has no inspectable SOS complexity source.

assumptions_latex: \(v_d\) contains all \(N=\binom{n+d}{d}\) monomials of degree at most \(d\).
No correlative-sparsity or symmetry decomposition is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A dense Gram model has \(N(N+1)/2\) matrix variables and up to \(\binom{n+2d}{2d}\) coefficient-matching equations.

notation.meaning: Dense monomial basis through degree one-half of the polynomial degree.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: dense symmetric storage and degree-bounded coefficient counts follow directly from the full monomial representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Size boundary caused by retaining the complete monomial support and one undecomposed semidefinite block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With the full monomial vector \(v_d\), the identity \(p=v_d^\mathsf TQv_d\) uses one positive-semidefinite block of order \(N=\binom{n+d}{d}\). The symmetric matrix \(Q\) has \(N(N+1)/2\) independent entries, while coefficient matching can involve every monomial through degree \(2d\), giving at most \(M=\binom{n+2d}{2d}\) affine equations. When the support and interaction graph admit no valid block decomposition, these dense dimensions cannot be reduced by sparsity splitting without changing the formulation. They constitute the dense-support representation barrier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without exploitable sparsity or symmetry, SOS modeling requires one full Gram block and coefficient equations for essentially every monomial through the target degree.
knowledge_statements.title: Dense-Support Barrier

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits the leaf, and the dense block size and upper bound on coefficient equations are correct. The stronger assertion that the dimensions cannot be reduced by sparsity splitting depends on the precise support or interaction graph and permitted reformulations; it requires a dedicated sparse-SOS source and sharper hypotheses.

assumptions_latex: An order-\(d\) dense SOS relaxation in \(n\) variables has Gram order \(N_d=\binom{n+d}{d}\).
The relaxation bounds \(L_d\) satisfy \(L_d\le L_{d+1}\le f^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Increasing \(d\) can tighten the certified lower bound, but changes dense Gram storage from \(\Theta(N_d^2)\) to \(\Theta(N_{d+1}^2)\); no finite accuracy rate follows from monotonicity alone.

notation.meaning: Certified lower bound at order d.
Dense Gram order at relaxation order d.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nested SOS relaxations give monotone bounds while the binomial Gram dimension quantifies representation growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic dense SOS hierarchy tradeoff; it asserts monotonic improvement but no universal convergence rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nested order-\(d\) SOS relaxations, feasibility of every order-\(d\) certificate at order \(d+1\) gives \(L_d\le L_{d+1}\le f^*\). The corresponding dense Gram order is \(N_d=\binom{n+d}{d}\), so matrix storage is \(\Theta(N_d^2)\) before accounting for linear-system and factorization costs. Raising \(d\) may therefore improve the certified optimality gap \(f^*-L_d\) while sharply increasing representation size. Monotonicity alone supplies neither a finite \(d\) achieving a prescribed tolerance nor a universal rate relating \(f^*-L_d\) to \(N_d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Higher SOS orders can improve certified bounds, but their Gram matrices grow combinatorially, and monotonicity by itself gives no universal accuracy-versus-size rate.
knowledge_statements.title: Accuracy–Scalability Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the tradeoff leaf, and the conditional conclusions follow from the explicitly assumed nested bounds and dense Gram dimensions. However, the hierarchy producing L_d, the optimization value f^*, and the hypotheses ensuring nestedness are not specified, and no hierarchy source is supplied. The claim about absence of a universal accuracy rate also needs a precise scoped source.
